definition: The revival of the LSTM with exponential gating and a matrix memory variant (mLSTM) that parallelizes training, scaled competitively into the billions of parameters.
details: The revival of the LSTM with exponential gating and a matrix memory variant (mLSTM) that parallelizes training, scaled competitively into the billions of parameters. Evidence that the recurrent design space was abandoned early rather than exhausted.

explainer.lead: xLSTM is a revival of the LSTM with exponential gating and a matrix memory variant (mLSTM) that parallelizes training, scaled competitively into the billions of parameters. It matters as evidence that the recurrent design space was abandoned early rather than exhausted.

tiers.eli5: It is an old memory-based design for sequence models, rebuilt so it can train on modern hardware and compete at large scale.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use the mLSTM matrix memory variant to parallelize training, which classic LSTMs could not do well. The pitfall is that the parallel training path depends on the specific variant, so naive LSTM implementations gain nothing.
tiers.paperLevel: An LSTM variant using exponential gating and a matrix-memory mLSTM that enables parallel training, scaled to billions of parameters. Competitive results at that scale are claimed, but the design has not displaced attention-based models generally.

explainer.example: A research team scales an xLSTM to billions of parameters and trains it in parallel, matching far larger recurrent setups that once trained only sequentially.
